reuse.why: All month-wide actions reuse getBulkBudgetCategories, and the new action also reuses averageToBudget, sheet access, batching, and undo registration.

duplication.why: Eligibility and amount-sign decisions remain shared, with no substantive duplicated logic introduced.

placement.why: Selection policy and budget calculations stay in budget/actions.ts, while method registration stays in budget/app.ts.

scope.why: The changes address the requested actions and exclusions, although adding goal_def to getBudgetData is unnecessary because eligibility is determined separately.

maintainability.why: The shared selector keeps future policy changes localized, with only minor cleanup needed around the unused query field and the increasingly general averageToBudget name.

bypasses_abstraction.where: Every affected month-wide action uses getBulkBudgetCategories, and setLastMonthSpending uses the existing shared sign conversion.

disguised_duplication.where: The diff extends shared eligibility logic rather than reproducing it in individual actions.

abstraction_drift.where: getBulkBudgetCategories replaces includeHidden with includeHiddenCategories and adds one combined template/fixed-group exclusion branch; these express requested shared policy without consumer-specific exceptions or bypasses.
